 Order

This appeal by the claimants under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is arising out of the award dated 06.03.2020 passed by 3 rd Additional Member, MACT, Betul in MACC No.387/2018 seeking enhancement of compensation amount awarded by the Tribunal.

2. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that Tribunal has assessed deceased's' income on the lower side, whereas, deceased's income should have been assessed on the basis of minimum wages as notified for skilled Labour.

On the date of accident, minimum wages of a skilled labour were Rs.
9,560/- per month.
Hence, compensation should have been determined by taking into consideration, deceased's monthly income as Rs.9,560/-.
On above grounds, it is urged that amount awarded by the Tribunal be suitably enhanced.
3. Learned counsel for the respondent-Insurance Company has submitted that compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and proper and no enhancement is required.
Hence, appeal filed by appellant be dismissed.

4. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused record of the case.
5.
Short issue involved in the case is deceased's monthly income.
As per findings recorded by Tribunal in para-19 of impugned award, Tribunal has held deceased a skilled labour considering him as a Tailor.
Therefore, in view of above, it would be just and proper to determine deceased's monthly income on the basis of minimum wages as fixed for a skilled labour under minimum wages Act.
In the instant case, accident occurred on 15.07.2018 and as per notification issued under minimum wages Act, monthly wages of a skilled labour were Rs.9,560/- on the date of accident.

If monthly wages Rs.9,560/- are multiplied by 12, then, deceased's annual income comes to Rs.9560 x 12 = Rs.1,14,720 and 25% of future prospect is added, then, annual income would be Rs.
143,400/-
7.
In the instant case, there is no dispute with respect to multiplier to be applied and deduction to be made under personal and living expenses.

In the instant case, one fourth (Rs.35,850/-) is to be deducted for personal and living expenses and remaining amount is to be multiplied by 13, then,
total dependency amount would be Rs.1,43,400-Rs.35,850/- = Rs.107,550/-x 13 = Rs.13,98,150/-
8.
In the instant case, Tribunal has awarded Rs.10,23,750/- as loss of dependency, whereas, in the instant case, loss of dependency comes to Rs.13,98,150/-.

Therefore, appellants are entitled to enhanced amount of i.e Rs.13,98,150 - Rs.10,23,750/- = Rs. 3,74,400/-.
9.
Enhanced amount of Rs. 3,74,400/- shall carry interest at the rate awarded by the Tribunal.
Other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact.
10. Appeal partly allowed to the extent as indicated above.
